n52a961cf0dd.s: Mutation breeding, a non-GMO approach, is associated with how many Trombay varieties linked to climate resilience?
n52a961cf0dd.x: Mutation breeding is a non-GMO approach, and 71 Trombay varieties are associated with climate resilience.

nf33d64d55fa.s: In the CRISPR-Cas9 system, which component acts as the molecular scissors?
nf33d64d55fa.x: Cas9 cuts the DNA and is the molecular scissors; the guide RNA only acts as the navigator.

nbiology-43-1.s: In the classic GMO application, the human insulin gene is put into which of the following to produce insulin?
nbiology-43-1.x: The human insulin gene is put into bacteria, which then make insulin.

nbiology-41-5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about CRISPR-Cas9?
o: It can be used to correct genetic defects
It can be used to improve crops
Its guide RNA acts as the molecular scissors
nbiology-41-5.x: Cas9 is the molecular scissors and the guide RNA is the navigator; CRISPR can fix genetic defects and improve crops, and it raises ethical concerns.

n2689252c1db.s: Bt cotton is claimed to reduce pesticide use mainly because the plant:
o: Produces its own insecticidal Bt toxin
n2689252c1db.x: Bt cotton carries a Bacillus thuringiensis gene and makes its own insecticidal toxin, so less pesticide is sprayed.

n78e2f188039.s: Which site-directed nuclease category uses a template but introduces no foreign DNA?
n78e2f188039.x: SDN-2 uses a template but adds no foreign DNA and is exempt under the 2022 guidelines; SDN-1 uses no template and SDN-3 inserts foreign DNA.

n72ad08b5445.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the risks of Bt toxins and other engineered traits?
o: They may affect pollinators and natural enemies of pests
They may affect soil nematodes and microbes
Lasting persistence of Bt proteins in soil is the proven main GM risk
n72ad08b5445.x: Bt proteins degrade in soil and lasting persistence is not proven; gene flow is the main GM risk. Non-target harm to pollinators, soil life and aquatic organisms is a real concern.

n00d986e6c59.s: Which of the following is a function of the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee?
o: Fixing the maximum retail price of commercial seeds
Taking punitive action at the State level
Field-level monitoring at the district level
Approving large-scale use of hazardous microorganisms and recombinants
n00d986e6c59.x: GEAC clears field trials, environmental release, commercial cultivation and large-scale use of hazardous microorganisms and recombinants; seed MRP is not its job.

n144497fcb27.s: Under the Rules, 1989, which body approves the environmental release and commercial use of GM crops?
n144497fcb27.x: GEAC under MoEFCC approves environmental release and commercial use; RCGM under DBT only monitors research and advises GEAC.

nff4cbdc2dd4.s: The initial commercial approval of Bt cotton in India in 2002 covered how many MAHYCO hybrids?
nff4cbdc2dd4.x: Three MAHYCO hybrids were approved for three years; Bt cotton remains the only GM crop commercially cultivated in India.

n97a61da527c.s: Which genome-editing category is transgenic and remains under full GM regulatory control in India?
n97a61da527c.x: SDN-3 inserts foreign DNA and stays fully regulated; SDN-1 and SDN-2 make small edits without foreign DNA and are exempt under the 2022 guidelines.

nbd0da3d9d5e.s: Which of the following is an objection raised by farmers against GURT or terminator seeds?
nbd0da3d9d5e.x: Farmers object to dependence on companies, recurring seed costs and the loss of seed-saving.

n4d701804137.s: Cartagena, after which the Protocol on Biosafety is named, is a city in:
n4d701804137.x: Cartagena is in Colombia; the Protocol is supplementary to the Convention on Biological Diversity.

nenvironment-6-3.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Eco-Sensitive Zone – Activities regulated, not necessarily prohibited
nenvironment-6-3.x: Activities in Eco-Sensitive Zones are regulated rather than banned. NGT comes from the NGT Act 2010, CGWA from Section 3(3) of EPA and CPCB from the Water Act 1974.

n5fc9b29218a.s: Binnig and Rohrer, who built the Scanning Tunnelling Microscope in 1981, received the Nobel Prize in Physics in:
n5fc9b29218a.x: The STM was made in 1981 and Binnig and Rohrer won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1986.

nchemistry-6-11.s: In diamond's tetrahedral network, each carbon atom is bonded to how many other carbon atoms?
nchemistry-6-11.x: Each carbon in diamond bonds to four others at the corners of a tetrahedron, giving a rigid 3D network.

nchemistry-6-3.s: Graphite is soft and slippery because its layers are held together by:
nchemistry-6-3.x: Graphite's layers are held only by weak van der Waals forces, so they slide over each other.

nchemistry-6-10.s: Hollow cylinders of rolled graphene are known as:
nchemistry-6-10.x: Carbon nanotubes are rolled graphene cylinders; fullerene C60 is a hollow spherical cage of 60 carbon atoms.

nchemistry-6-15.s: Diamond is an electrical insulator because it:
o: Is a hollow cage of 60 atoms
nchemistry-6-15.x: Diamond insulates because it has no free electrons; its good heat conduction comes from lattice vibrations, a separate fact.

nchemistry-6-18.s: Which form of carbon is a hollow cage of 60 atoms?
nchemistry-6-18.x: Fullerene C60 is the 60-atom cage; graphene is the strong single-atom sheet, graphite the slippery lubricant and diamond the hardest natural substance.

n8d67cad57cb.s: In India, dual-use concerns of nanotechnology are addressed under the:
n8d67cad57cb.x: India has no dedicated nano law; dual-use concerns come under the SCOMET list, while DGFASLI covers occupational risk and FSSAI food.

new.s: In which year was the first GMO produced?
new.x: The first GMO dates to 1973; 1982 is Humulin, 1994 Flavr Savr and 2002 Bt cotton approval in India.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Bt cotton was approved in India in 2002. Humulin came in 1982, Flavr Savr in 1994 and CRISPR-Cas9 was shown in 2012.

new.s: In the plasmid vector pBR322, the letters 'BR' stand for:
new.x: pBR322 is an early E. coli vector: p = plasmid, BR = Bolivar and Rodriguez.

new.s: Which organism is called 'Nature's genetic engineer'?
new.x: Agrobacterium tumefaciens is nature's genetic engineer; its disarmed Ti plasmid carries T-DNA into plants.

new.s: The second-generation Bt cotton, Bollgard II, was introduced in:
new.x: Bollgard I came in 2002 and Bollgard II, with Cry1Ac + Cry2Ab, in 2006.

new.s: Which sucking pests have risen as a problem in Bt cotton fields?
new.x: Bt cotton has seen a rise of sucking pests such as whitefly and mealybug, besides pink bollworm resistance.

new.s: Between 2002 and 2023, Bt cotton yield in India rose from 190 kg/ha to about:
new.x: Bt cotton yield rose from 190 to 480 kg/ha between 2002 and 2023.

new.s: Bacillus thuringiensis has been sprayed as a microbial insecticide since:
new.x: Bt, a Gram-positive soil bacterium, has been used as a sprayed microbial insecticide since 1920.

new.s: A 2025-26 study found illegal HTBt cotton on about what share of the cotton area in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Illegal HTBt cotton covered about 15-18% of cotton area in AP and 27-30% in Telangana.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about HTBt cotton:
1. It combines the Bt trait with glyphosate tolerance.
2. It is approved for commercial cultivation in India.
3. Labour shortage and cheap glyphosate weeding drive its spread.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: HTBt cotton adds glyphosate tolerance to Bt and spreads because of labour shortage and cheap weeding, but it is not approved and is illegal.

new.s: GM mustard DMH-11 was developed at Delhi University's CGMCP under:
new.x: DMH-11 was developed by Delhi University's CGMCP led by Deepak Pental.

new.s: Bt brinjal, recommended by GEAC in 2009, was put under a moratorium in:
new.x: GEAC recommended Bt brinjal in 2009 and Jairam Ramesh imposed a moratorium in 2010.

new.s: Who received the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for CRISPR-Cas9?
new.x: Doudna and Charpentier showed CRISPR-Cas9 in 2012 and won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2020.

new.s: ICAR's indigenous, smaller alternative to Cas9 for genome editing is:
new.x: TnpB, developed by ICAR, is an indigenous and smaller alternative to Cas9.

new.s: The genome-edited rice DRR Dhan 100 (Kamala) was developed by:
new.x: Kamala (DRR Dhan 100) comes from ICAR-IIRR, Hyderabad, from Samba Mahsuri; Pusa DST Rice 1 is from ICAR-IARI.

new.s: Pusa DST Rice 1 was made by editing which variety bred at Maruteru, Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Pusa DST Rice 1 is edited MTU1010, a variety bred at Maruteru, AP; Kamala is from Samba Mahsuri.

new.s: India's first genome-edited rice varieties were released in:
new.x: India became the first to release genome-edited rice on 4 May 2025; 2022 is the year SDN-1/2 were exempted.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about genetic medicine?
o: Gene therapy alters, replaces or corrects defective genes
Hepatitis B and HPV vaccines are recombinant vaccines
Mitochondrial replacement therapy is called the three-parent baby technique
new.x: Pharmacogenomics relates genes to drug response; gene silencing is RNAi.

new.s: CDSCO rules on gene therapy in India came in:
new.x: Gene therapy alters or corrects defective genes, and CDSCO issued rules on it in 2023.

new.s: Golden Rice was developed by:
new.x: Golden Rice was developed by Ingo Potrykus and Peter Beyer.

new.s: How many biofortified crop varieties did ICAR release in one year?
new.x: ICAR released 34 biofortified varieties in one year; 71 is the count of Trombay mutation-bred varieties.

new.s: AquAdvantage, whose escapees may out-compete wild stock, is a genetically modified:
new.x: AquAdvantage is a GM salmon; escapees may out-compete wild fish.

new.s: With a gene drive, what share of GM mosquito offspring inherit the trait?
new.x: Gene drives make more than 90% of offspring inherit the trait, against the normal 50%.

new.s: Which country has the largest area under GM crops?
new.x: The USA leads, followed by Brazil, Argentina, Canada and India; the top five hold over 90% of world GM area.

new.s: In global GM crop area, India ranks:
new.x: India is fifth after the USA, Brazil, Argentina and Canada.

new.s: The Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety was adopted in 2000 at:
new.x: The Protocol was adopted in 2000 at Montreal and entered into force in 2003.

new.s: Movement of transgenes through pollen into wild relatives can give rise to:
new.x: Gene flow by pollen into non-GM crops and wild relatives can create superweeds and alter gene pools.

new.s: Antibiotic-resistance marker genes in GM crops raise the fear of:
new.x: Antibiotic-resistance markers raise fear that resistance may spread to pathogens.

new.s: Which GURT type switches a trait on or off by applying a chemical?
new.x: T-GURT (traitor) switches a trait by a chemical and is at research stage; V-GURT (terminator) gives sterile seeds.

new.s: The US patent on turmeric for wound healing was revoked after a challenge by:
new.x: The 1995 US turmeric patent was revoked after CSIR challenged it.

new.s: India won the neem biopiracy case at the:
new.x: India won the neem (anti-fungal) case at the European Patent Office.

new.s: The 1997 US patent on basmati rice, challenged by CSIR, was held by:
new.x: RiceTec of the USA held the 1997 basmati patent; key claims were disallowed after CSIR's challenge.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Hoodia (P57) is an appetite suppressant shared with the San people. Turmeric was for wound healing, neem anti-fungal and basmati was RiceTec's patent.

new.s: The Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (2001) was set up by:
new.x: TKDL was created in 2001 by CSIR and the Ministry of AYUSH.

new.s: TKDL helps against biopiracy mainly by giving patent offices:
new.x: TKDL gives patent offices prior-art evidence that the knowledge already exists.

new.s: From 1 March 2021, imported major food crops into India need a:
new.x: Since 1 March 2021, imported major food crops must carry a 'non-GM cum GM-free' certificate.

new.s: India's draft GM labelling applies to foods containing GM ingredients of:
new.x: The draft labelling rule covers foods with 1% or more GM ingredient.

new.s: The BRAI Bill, 2013 lapsed with the end of the:
new.x: The BRAI Bill proposed a single biotech regulator and lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha.

new.s: In July 2024, which body directed the Centre to frame a national GM crop policy?
new.x: In its July 2024 split verdict on DMH-11, both Supreme Court judges directed the Centre to frame a national GM crop policy.

new.s: The Biological Weapons Convention entered into force in:
new.x: The BWC was opened in 1972 and entered into force in 1975; India is a Party.

new.s: Serious airborne agents such as TB are handled at which biosafety level?
new.x: BSL-3 is for serious airborne agents like TB; BSL-4 is for lethal agents with no cure like Ebola.

new.s: Field trials of GM crops in India are conducted as:
new.x: GM field trials are run as Biosafety Research Level trials, BRL-I and BRL-II.

new.s: Since 2010, what has been mandatory for conducting GM crop field trials?
new.x: Since 2010 a State NOC is mandatory for field trials, and several States refuse it.

new.s: Which committee under the Rules, 1989 can inspect, investigate and take punitive action at the State level?
new.x: The SBCC acts at State level with powers to inspect, investigate and punish; DLC monitors at district level.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the competent authorities under the Rules, 1989?
new.x: The six competent authorities are RDAC, IBSC, RCGM, GEAC, SBCC and DLC; FSSAI is not one of them.

new.s: GEAC functions under which ministry?
new.x: GEAC is under MoEFCC; it is RCGM that works under DBT.

new.s: The Supreme Court-appointed Technical Expert Committee of 2013 recommended:
o: A 10-year moratorium on GM field trials
new.x: The 2013 Technical Expert Committee recommended a 10-year moratorium on field trials.

new.s: GEAC cleared the environmental release of GM mustard DMH-11 in:
new.x: GEAC cleared DMH-11 in 2017 but the Ministry withheld it; environmental release was cleared on 18 October 2022.

new.s: Bt brinjal carries which gene against the fruit and shoot borer?
new.x: Bt brinjal uses the Cry1Ac gene against the fruit and shoot borer.

new.s: The Flavr Savr tomato achieved delayed ripening using:
new.x: Flavr Savr used antisense polygalacturonase for delayed ripening.

new.s: In Novartis v Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court upheld the rejection of a patent on:
new.x: The SC upheld rejection of the Glivec (imatinib) patent under Section 3(d), which blocks evergreening.

new.s: Pusa Rice DST1 was produced by an SDN-1 knockout of which gene?
new.x: Pusa Rice DST1 is an SDN-1 DST gene knockout in MTU1010, giving drought and salinity tolerance.

new.s: GM mustard DMH-11 also carries herbicide tolerance through the:
new.x: DMH-11 carries the bar gene, which gives herbicide tolerance and fuels public resistance.

new.s: The Nano Mission approved in 2007 had an outlay of:
new.x: The Nano Mission (DST) was approved on 3 May 2007 with Rs 1,000 crore for five years.

new.s: Phase II of the Nano Mission, with Rs 650 crore, was approved in:
new.x: Phase II was approved in 2014 for the 12th Plan with Rs 650 crore.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about nanotechnology tools:
1. The STM images only conducting surfaces.
2. The AFM works on non-conductors too.
3. Lithography is a bottom-up method.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The STM needs conductors, while the AFM (1986) also images non-conductors. Lithography is top-down.

new.s: Lithography, milling and etching are examples of which approach to nanomaterial synthesis?
new.x: Top-down methods cut bulk material down, such as lithography, milling and etching.

new.s: Aerosols and nanocoatings belong to which generation of nanoproducts?
new.x: Passive nanostructures such as aerosols, colloids and coatings form the first generation.

new.s: Molecular manufacturing is an example of which generation of nanoproducts?
new.x: The fourth generation, molecular nanosystems, covers molecular manufacturing.

new.s: Bendable graphene-based wearable sensors were developed by:
new.x: IISc and C-DAC developed bendable graphene wearable sensors.

new.s: Silver-nanoparticle wound dressings that cut infections by about 60% were developed by:
new.x: CSIR-CGCRI developed silver-nanoparticle wound dressings.

new.s: 'Nano-cups' for heat-based cancer therapy are associated with:
new.x: INST Mohali developed nano-cups for heat-based cancer therapy and nano-formulations for Parkinson's.

new.s: The Guidelines for Evaluation of Nano-based Agri-input and Food Products (2020) were issued by DBT with:
new.x: The 2020 guidelines were brought out by DBT, the Agriculture Ministry and FSSAI.

new.s: Quantum dots are semiconductor nanostructures about how large?
new.x: Quantum dots are about 1.5-10 nm and show size-set colour.

new.s: A fullerene C60 molecule is made of:
new.x: C60, the buckyball, is a cage of 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons.

new.s: Quantum wells, wires and dots confine electrons in how many dimensions, respectively?
new.x: Wells confine in 1, wires in 2 and dots in 3 dimensions (2D, 1D and 0D structures).

new.s: Which material is believed to be harder than diamond?
new.x: Wurtzite boron nitride is believed harder than diamond.

new.s: Kroto, Curl and Smalley received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for fullerene in:
new.x: Fullerene C60 was found in 1985 and the Chemistry Nobel came in 1996.

new.s: The 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics for graphene went to:
new.x: Geim and Novoselov of Manchester won the 2010 Physics Nobel for graphene.

new.s: The 1959 lecture 'There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom' was given by:
new.x: Feynman's 1959 lecture is the origin of the idea; Taniguchi coined the term in 1974.

new.s: India's first nano-cellulose plant at ICAR-CIRCOT, Mumbai uses:
new.x: ICAR-CIRCOT's plant makes nano-cellulose from cotton linters and wastes.

new.s: IIT Bombay's perovskite-silicon tandem solar cell has reached an efficiency of:
new.x: IIT Bombay's perovskite-silicon tandem cell reached 27.3% efficiency.

new.s: IFFCO's liquid Nano Urea has a particle size of about:
new.x: Nano Urea is a liquid with 20-50 nm particles used as a foliar spray.

new.s: Nano DAP is meant for:
new.x: Nano DAP, notified on 2 March 2023, is used for seed treatment and foliar spray.

new.s: One nanometre equals:
new.x: 1 nm is one billionth of a metre, 10^-9 m; nanoparticles span 10^-9 to 10^-7 m.
